original_value: Leaf chlorophyll content (LCC) is a pivotal parameter in the monitoring of agriculture and carbon cycle modeling at regional and global scales. ENVISAT MERIS and Sentinel-3 OLCI data are suitable for use in the global monitoring of LCC because of their spectral specifications (covering red-edge bands), wide field of view and short revisit times. Generally, remote sensing approaches for LCC retrieval consist of statistically- and physically-based models. The physical approaches for LCC estimation require the use of radiative transfer models (RTMs), which are more robust and transferrable than empirical models. However, the operational retrieval of LCC at large scales is affected by the large variability in canopy structures and soil backgrounds. In this study, we proposed an improved look-up-table (LUT) approach to retrieve LCC by combining multiple canopy structures and soil backgrounds to deal with the ill-posed inversion problem caused by the lack of prior knowledge on canopy structure and soil-background reflectance. Firstly, the PROSAIL-D model was used to simulate canopy spectra with diverse imaging gometrics, canopy structures, soil backgrounds and leaf biochemical contents, and the canopy spectra were resampled according to the spectral response functions of ENVISAT MERIS and Sentinel-3 OLCI instruments. Then, an LUT that included 25 sub-LUTs corresponding to five types of canopy structure and five types of soil background was generated for LCC estimation. The mean of the best eight solutions, rather than the single best solution with the smallest RMSE value, was selected as the retrieval of each sub-LUT. The final inversion result was obtained by calculating the mean value of the 25 sub-LUTs. Finally, the improved LUT approach was tested using simulations, field measurements and ENVISAT MERIS satellite data. A simulation using spectral bands from the MERIS and Sentinel-3 OLCI simulation datasets yielded an R2 value of 0.81 and an RMSE value of 10.1 μg cm−2. Validation performed well with field-measured canopy spectra and MERIS imagery giving RMSE values of 9.9 μg cm−2 for wheat and 9.6 μg cm−2 for soybean using canopy spectra and 8.6 μg cm−2 for soybean using MERIS data. The comparison with traditional chlorophyll-sensitive indices showed that our improved LUT approach gave the best performance for all cases. Therefore, these promising results are directly applicable to the use of ENVISAT MERIS and Sentinel-3 OLCI data for monitoring of crop LCC at a regional or global scale.

result.paraphrase: Leaf chlorophyll content (LCC) is a key variable for agricultural monitoring and carbon-cycle modeling at regional and global scales. Because of their spectral characteristics, including red-edge bands, broad swath, and short revisit intervals, ENVISAT MERIS and Sentinel-3 OLCI data are well suited to global LCC monitoring. In general, remote-sensing methods for LCC retrieval are based on either statistical or physical models. Physical approaches for LCC estimation rely on radiative transfer models (RTMs), which are more robust and transferable than empirical models. However, large-scale operational LCC retrieval is challenged by the strong variability in canopy structure and soil background. In this study, we developed an improved look-up-table (LUT) method for LCC retrieval that combines multiple canopy structures and soil backgrounds to address the ill-posed inversion problem caused by limited prior knowledge of canopy structure and soil-background reflectance. First, the PROSAIL-D model was used to simulate canopy spectra under different imaging geometries, canopy structures, soil backgrounds, and leaf biochemical contents, and the spectra were then resampled according to the spectral response functions of ENVISAT MERIS and Sentinel-3 OLCI instruments. Next, an LUT consisting of 25 sub-LUTs, corresponding to five canopy-structure types and five soil-background types, was built for LCC estimation. For each sub-LUT, the retrieval was defined as the mean of the best eight solutions rather than the single best solution with the lowest RMSE. The final inversion result was obtained as the average of the 25 sub-LUTs. The improved LUT approach was then evaluated with simulations, field measurements, and ENVISAT MERIS satellite data. Using MERIS and Sentinel-3 OLCI simulated spectral bands, the simulation produced an R2 of 0.81 and an RMSE of 10.1 μg cm−2. Validation performed well: with field-measured canopy spectra and MERIS imagery, RMSE values were 9.9 μg cm−2 for wheat and 9.6 μg cm−2 for soybean using canopy spectra, and 8.6 μg cm−2 for soybean using MERIS data. Compared with traditional chlorophyll-sensitive indices, the improved LUT approach achieved the best performance in all cases. These encouraging results indicate that ENVISAT MERIS and Sentinel-3 OLCI data can be directly used for regional or global monitoring of crop LCC.
